scenes.headline: How a decision model hears a video clip
scenes.sub: Cloudflare's open Clef-omni, and how Microsoft timed its closed rival.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cadenza! Two decision models shipped on the same day. One hears sound and video, with open weights. The other is closed, and claims to be fastest.

scenes.text: Clef-omni keeps Qwen's audio and vision encoders untouched and trains the text decoder to carry their evidence to a scoring head.
scenes.say: Clef-omni's trick is what it leaves alone. The ears and eyes are Qwen's, unchanged. Only the reader was trained.

steps.say: Pictures, sound and video frames go through Qwen's own encoders. A video's soundtrack shares its timeline.
They join one prompt with the state and every option, read once. Each token visits eight experts.
Nothing is generated. The hidden states over each option are kept.
Clef's joint head scores every option of every question together.

left.title: Bit for bit Qwen
left.say: Against the base, the encoders, routers and speech generator are identical.

right.title: Trained by Cloudflare
right.say: What moved is the text decoder's attention and experts, plus the new head.

scenes.label: Clef-omni on the independent Decision Index, 27th of 117
scenes.say: On the community board, Clef-omni ranks twenty-seventh, and drops much further on private tests than most.

scenes.credit: Microsoft's launch chart, from the video
scenes.title: Microsoft's speed claim

steps.say: Microsoft's chart puts its model first on speed, at eighty-five milliseconds.
The footnote says the other rows are adjusted medians, and Microsoft measured its own inside the same region.

parts.note: timed on the benchmark's own GPU
parts.say: The benchmark times open models on its own GPU, with no network in the way.

parts.note: a stand-in for network and queueing
parts.say: So it doubles that and adds a hundred and fifty milliseconds, to sit beside hosted services.

scenes.title: Before the adjustment
scenes.note: Microsoft's figure measured in its own region
scenes.say: Take the surcharge off, and a four billion model answered faster. The chart sets a network-free number against open models charged for a network.

scenes.text: Ask which parts a model actually trained, and which clock each latency was measured on.
scenes.say: So read the weights to see what was trained, and read the footnote to see what was timed.

recap: Same Clef head reads every input
Latency claims need the same clock
scenes.say: Qwen's encoders, Clef's head, and a speed chart with two clocks.
